name: The Internet
description: How a research network of four computers became the internet: ARPANET, email, the web, Wi-Fi and beyond.

checkpoints.name: ARPANET
checkpoints.note: Researchers in America and Britain devise packet switching, and the US funds ARPANET to link its computers. Telnet, email and file transfer appear, and Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn sketch TCP/IP in 1974.

checkpoints.name: Email, Usenet and bulletin boards
checkpoints.note: Ethernet joins computers in buildings, Usenet and bulletin boards let strangers talk, and ARPANET adopts TCP/IP. DNS and SMTP give the net its names and its mail.

checkpoints.name: The internet opens up
checkpoints.note: The NSFNET links universities, while services such as CompuServe and Minitel bring the public online by modem. IRC and Gopher give an early taste of chat and browsing.

checkpoints.name: The World Wide Web
checkpoints.note: Tim Berners-Lee's web, with HTML and HTTP, and the Mosaic and Netscape browsers make the internet easy to use. Search engines and encryption follow, and millions come online.

checkpoints.name: Always online
checkpoints.note: Wi-Fi and phone networks put the net in every pocket, IPv6 makes room for more devices, and satellites such as Starlink reach places that cables never will.
